correctness.rationale: The barycentric orbit lemma is applied to vertices representing fan edges. Every two-element spoke orbit is inadmissible since the spokes meet at the apex. At even n=2m, each rim edge-reflection orbit O_i for 1<=i<=m is an admissible matching and distinct orbits conflict exactly at neighboring indices, producing Ind(P_m). At odd n=2m+1 the central paired rim orbit meets at the middle rim vertex and is inadmissible, while the one fixed central spoke is compatible with every remaining m-1 rim pair, giving Cone(Ind(P_(m-1))); n=3 yields a single point. In path independence complexes, neighborhood domination N(1) subset N(3) deletes vertex 3 and leaves K2 disjoint union P_(j-3), so the complex suspends every three steps. Base path cases j=1,2,3 give contractible, S^0, S^0, hence the stated periodic sphere dimension (including even n=4 two points) without extrapolation. Independently constructed the original fan-edge conflict graph and involution and checked exact orbit quotient graph isomorphism for every n=3..20 (18 cases); unbounded conclusion follows from explicit edge incidences and fold recurrence.
